title: GSArch: Breaking Memory Barriers in 3D Gaussian Splatting Training via Architectural Support
problem: 3D Gaussian Splatting (3DGS) training is bottlenecked by three memory system inefficiencies: redundant off-chip DRAM loads for large 'hot' Gaussians accessed repeatedly across pixels, expensive atomic write operations during gradient accumulation, and severe bank conflicts during on-chip buffer reads during backward propagation.
motivation: Online 3DGS training for dynamic environment perception (autonomous driving, embodied AI) requires much higher training throughput than current GPU implementations provide; existing 3DGS accelerators (e.g., GSCore) address only rendering, not the backward pass.
method: GSArch introduces three architectural mechanisms targeting the three bottlenecks: (1) Hybrid memory management that classifies Gaussians as 'hot' (large, high pixel overlap, repeatedly loaded) or 'cold' and caches hot Gaussians in a fast on-chip buffer to eliminate redundant DRAM fetches; (2) Gradient informativeness filtering that identifies low-contribution gradients and skips their atomic write operations during backward propagation; (3) A rearrangement unit that packs conflicting on-chip memory read requests into non-conflicting bundles to eliminate bank conflicts. These techniques combine to accelerate the backward pass of 3DGS training.
key_novelty: Gaussian 'hotness' classification for hybrid on-chip/off-chip memory management that eliminates the dominant redundant DRAM load pattern in 3DGS training backward propagation.
contributions: Characterization of 3DGS training inefficiencies: redundant DRAM loads, atomic write bottlenecks, and on-chip bank conflicts.
Hybrid memory management classifying Gaussians into hot/cold categories with on-chip buffering of hot Gaussians.
Gradient informativeness filtering to skip low-contribution atomic gradient writes.
Rearrangement unit eliminating on-chip buffer bank conflicts; up to 6.49x speedup over A100 and 15.42x over Jetson AGX Xavier with negligible quality loss.

metrics.speedup: Up to 6.49x over A100 GPU; up to 15.42x over Jetson AGX Xavier
metrics.energy_or_tops_w: Substantially lower energy consumption (not quantified in abstract)

limitations: The hot/cold Gaussian classification threshold tuning strategy and its sensitivity to scene complexity or Gaussian density are not discussed.
primary_theme: Architectural support for memory-efficient 3D Gaussian Splatting training via hot/cold Gaussian buffering
